USA.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Use the Osaka G20 meeting to restart talks without imposing List 4 or rolling back existing Section 301 duties. Keep the 25% tariffs on ~$250B and the Huawei Entity List in place as leverage, and insist China return to the draft structural/enforcement text it walked back in May. Do not trade a full Huawei lifeline or tariff rollback for purchase promises alone; a no-new-tariff pause is the most we should offer to get negotiators back in the room.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is real but not high. After the May 10 List 3 hike to 25% and the May 16 Huawei listing, China raised duties on ~$60B of US goods, floated an unreliable-entity list, and signaled rare-earth leverage—hurting a politically sensitive export sector (soybeans near decade lows; USDA authorized up to $16B in farm aid on May 23). Markets priced a growth scare: the 10-year yield fell from 2.69% (end-2018) to 2.05% (June 26) and the 2-year (1.77%) sits well below the funds rate (2.38%). That is closer to the +0.5 “key export sector / political pressure” anchor than to opportunity, but it is not existential: Michigan sentiment is still 98.2, CPI is contained, industrial production is only modestly softer, and China’s own IP/reserves have not cracked. Escalating List 4 now would land on phones, apparel and other consumer goods with thin US substitution, likely kill talks (a person familiar told Reuters that new tariffs would mean talks are “dead”), and invite rare-earth or entity-list retaliation against US tech. Full concession is equally wrong: Washington’s stated ask is that Beijing restore the May draft, and Congress would punish a cheap Huawei rollback. With Trump and Xi already set to meet after the June 18 call, the aligned move is negotiate—hold current pressure, explore a ceasefire on further hikes, and reopen working-level talks.
key_factors: Osaka G20 meeting already teed up after the June 18 Trump-Xi call; US officials want talks restarted, not a signed deal
Existing leverage is already high: 25% on ~$250B (List 3 hiked May 10) plus Huawei Entity List (May 16)
List 4 (~$300B consumer goods) is proposed but not in force; imposing it now would tax US consumers and likely terminate negotiations
Farm-belt retaliation is the clearest US vulnerability: China hiked the $60B list; USDA announced up to $16B in aid; soybean prices near 10-year lows
Financial conditions tightened (10y -64bp; 2y below fed funds) but the real-side US economy is not in a tariff recession
China still has unused non-tariff tools (rare earths, unreliable-entity list) that would bite US tech if we escalate further
Structural/enforcement issues remain unresolved after the May breakdown; purchase-only concessions would not fix IP/tech-transfer

sources_cited.excerpt: List 3 tariff rate rises from 10% to 25%.
China announces it will raise retaliatory tariff rates on its ~$60B US-goods list (higher rates phased in; many effective June 1).
US Commerce Department adds Huawei and affiliates to the Entity List. US firms generally barred from selling to Huawei without a license.

Google suspends Huawei's access to Android updates / GMS; major US chip suppliers pause sales. Same day: Xi Jinping visits a rare-earth facility in Jiangxi (widely read as a signal on rare-earth leverage).
China announces it will establish an "unreliable entity list" targeting foreign firms that cut supplies to Chinese companies for non-commercial reasons.
Trump and Xi agree by phone to meet at the G20 in Osaka.
US 10-year yield latest 2.05 on 2019-06-26, down 0.64 (-23.8%) over the window.
US 2-year yield latest 1.77 on 2019-06-26 versus federal funds 2.38 — curve inverted vs policy rate.
Michigan consumer sentiment still 98.2 in June 2019 — no collapse in household confidence.
US hopes to relaunch talks after Osaka; not willing to arrive with concessions; a no-new-tariff gesture possible; person familiar: if they go with the tariffs, the trade talks are dead.
USDA authorized up to $16 billion in programs to offset retaliatory-tariff damage to US agriculture.
Proposed List 4 covers virtually all remaining Chinese-origin products including apparel, footwear, computers and other consumer electronics, excluding pharma, rare earths and critical minerals.

CHN.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: At Osaka, restart talks and seek a pause on the threatened ~$300B US tariff tranche and a longer Huawei licensing window, without signing the April enforcement text or making new purchase/structural commitments. Keep in place the June 1 retaliatory rates and the announced-but-unpopulated unreliable-entity list as leverage; do not fire rare-earth or named-firm countermeasures into the summit. The aim is a truce that preserves dignity and optionality, not a settlement on US terms.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is high, not existential. Since May the US raised List 3 from 10% to 25% (2019-05-10), covering ~$250B, and put Huawei and affiliates on the Entity List (2019-05-16), after which Google and major US chip suppliers paused sales (2019-05-20). That combination hits both the export machine and the national tech champion: Huawei's ~$105B franchise and a reported ~$30B two-year revenue hit sit on top of already-elevated tariffs, with Trump still threatening to tax the remaining ~$300B if Osaka fails. CNY weakened from ~6.73 to ~6.92 after the May breakdown (DEXCHUS/EXCHUS), which is FX pressure consistent with the +0.5 CHN anchor. It is not +1.0: June industrial production is still +6.3% YoY, merchandise exports are roughly flat, and reserves rose to ~$3.14T — the real economy is strained, not breaking. Opportunity (nationalism, rare-earth signaling at Jiangxi on 2019-05-20, Made-in-China autonomy) is real but does not offset Huawei plus the $300B overhang. Action should be negotiate, not escalate or concede. China already matched the May hike (2019-05-13) and announced an unreliable-entity list (2019-05-31); a further shot now would raise the odds the US implements the residual tariffs, which a person familiar with the talks said would kill negotiations. Conversely, conceding purchases or rolling back first would abandon Liu He's three May reservations (remove penalty tariffs, realistic purchase volumes, a balanced/dignified text) before the US has offered a matching path. The June 18 Trump–Xi call already scheduled an extended G20 meeting and working-level talks; US officials on 26 June said they hope to relaunch talks and might freeze new tariffs as a goodwill gesture but will not arrive with concessions. Meeting that opening — talk, hold existing counters, extract a pause — is the stance that matches a +0.45 threat without walking into either a technology/export shock or a humiliating April-text revival.
key_factors: List 3 now at 25% on ~$250B plus a live threat to tariff the remaining ~$300B if Osaka yields no progress
Huawei Entity List (May 16) plus Google/chip-supplier cutoff is firm-level targeting of the national 5G champion
CNY weakened sharply after the May breakdown; IP, exports, and reserves are strained but not in crisis
China already retaliated on ~$60B (June 1) and announced an unreliable-entity list — further escalation into the summit is surplus risk
June 18 call set a G20 meeting; both sides face pressure to resume talks without a ready final text
Liu He red lines (tariff removal, realistic purchases, balanced text) make pre-summit concession premature
